name: chocolate
notes: Theobromine and caffeine cause vomiting, tremors, tachycardia, and seizures; darker chocolate is more dangerous.

name: xylitol
notes: Causes rapid, life-threatening hypoglycemia and acute liver failure even in tiny amounts.

name: grapes
notes: Can cause acute kidney failure; toxic dose is unpredictable, so any ingestion is treated as dangerous.

name: onion
notes: Allium species damage red blood cells and cause hemolytic anemia; powdered forms are concentrated.

name: garlic
notes: More potent than onion; causes oxidative damage to red blood cells and anemia.

name: macadamia nuts
notes: Cause weakness, vomiting, tremors, and hyperthermia, typically within 12 hours.

name: alcohol
notes: Causes CNS depression, hypothermia, low blood sugar, and respiratory failure.

name: caffeine
notes: A methylxanthine like theobromine; causes hyperactivity, tachycardia, tremors, and seizures.

name: ibuprofen
notes: Human NSAID; causes stomach ulcers, GI bleeding, and kidney failure in dogs.

name: acetaminophen
notes: Causes liver damage and red blood cell injury; dogs lack the enzymes to process it safely.

name: naproxen
notes: Long-acting human NSAID with a very narrow safety margin; causes GI ulceration and kidney injury.

name: pseudoephedrine
notes: Stimulant that causes agitation, dangerously high heart rate and blood pressure, and tremors.

name: lily
notes: Highly nephrotoxic to cats; in dogs causes GI upset and, with some species, more serious effects.

name: sago palm
notes: All parts are toxic; the seeds especially cause severe liver failure and are often fatal.

name: azalea
notes: Grayanotoxins cause vomiting, drooling, weakness, abnormal heart rhythm, and collapse.

name: tulip
notes: Bulbs contain the most toxin; cause drooling, vomiting, and diarrhea.

name: oleander
notes: Contains cardiac glycosides; causes severe arrhythmias, GI signs, and can be fatal.

name: autumn crocus
notes: Causes severe vomiting, GI bleeding, organ damage, and bone marrow suppression.

name: antifreeze
notes: Sweet-tasting and rapidly fatal; causes acute kidney failure. Treat any suspected ingestion immediately.

name: rodenticide
notes: Depending on type, causes internal bleeding, brain swelling, or kidney failure; bring the packaging to the vet.

name: xylitol toothpaste
notes: Many human toothpastes contain xylitol; causes hypoglycemia and possible liver injury.

name: bleach
notes: Causes mouth and GI irritation, drooling, and vomiting; concentrated forms are corrosive.

name: slug bait
notes: Causes severe tremors and seizures ('shake and bake'); rapidly life-threatening.

name: marijuana
notes: Causes lethargy, wobbliness, dribbling urine, and low heart rate; edibles may also contain toxic chocolate or xylitol.

name: fertilizer
notes: Usually causes GI upset; some products with iron, herbicides, or pesticides are more serious.
